notes.text: The page states a definition of alpha by constructing Pi, tilde Pi and p from the action data. It defines the objects of Pi as the orbit set, writes the Isom sets in terms of the fibres and describes composition as evident. The canceled preliminary formula and the replacement object declaration are retained. This is an account of what the manuscript says, not a proof of the construction.

The central diagram and the following prose describe the projection of the unique point of Isom(z,z prime) to a pi-isomorphism carrying z to z prime. The right margin calls tilde Pi discrete over Pi, supplies a functor F and writes an equivalence with Pi subscript /F. The uncertain insertion contr. and the canceled old parenthesis remain visibly marked. Reader A performed no mathematical proof; the later limited main-reader check is recorded separately at N7.

The lower paragraph says that the action-group letter had not yet been used, then describes compatible actions on Pi and tilde Pi and a quotient passage. Its literal final target is read as lowercase pi from the graph, although the preceding sentences discuss capital Pi. This potential source slip is not silently repaired, and no claim about the mathematical validity of the sentence is made.

Both pencil page numerals are transcribed, with the hand unnamed. H’s page attribution, margin descriptions, quotation marks around descriptions and report of an unreadable line are editorial matter rather than extra manuscript words. The source graphic features they describe are reconstructed.

A small dark point is visible after the first orbit-set quotient, near native (647,360), in the main objects_pi crop. Its placement admits punctuation but is high enough to leave pen-speck uncertainty; an unsure point is retained. This is a low-confidence main-reader addition, not a resolved punctuation correction.

Limited main-reader mathematical check: a free pi-action makes each orbit Z_j a pi-torsor. Given z in Z_j and z-prime in Z_j-prime, gamma z maps to gamma z-prime. Freeness makes this well-defined, equivariance follows from the formula, the reverse formula gives an inverse, and transitivity gives uniqueness. This checks the local assertion about the unique pi-isomorphism; it does not prove the announced categorical equivalence. The ink independently shows the closely joined I+s of Isom. The manuscript’s cat. discrète is retained, with its marginal qualification sur Pi; no replacement by another category-theoretic term is made.

Graphic decisions follow the ink: dots over z in the replacement, Ens rather than Ob in the lower equality, a bare shaft between fibres, four suspension points after z prime, and unexpanded isom and Pi-auto---. The tuple’s compressed last entry is read as a after comparison with the explicitly named action map on scan017; it is not a correction of a clear relation sign. After main highlighted the extra low stroke, isom replaces Reader A’s initial iso; no detached period is supplied. The small-t position remains explicitly doubtful between baseline pt and p with raised t; the first reading retains Reader A’s baseline judgment.

Full second reading complete. Four material graphic/punctuation corrections and one certainty-only resolution are proposed. All seven original MARKS decisions remain unchanged. Fourteen of the fifteen accepted remaining doubts remain; only the tuple a/sim doubt is removed.

The input-tuple and central-parenthesis continuations each have two visible marks, represented by a point and short bar. The marginal F(j) continuation has three marks and the body z-prime continuation four; their counts are retained. The terminal marks in those latter groups are horizontally elongated, but no new mark is supplied or removed.

The named action datum a is a contextual reading of a graph admitting that hand formation, not correction of an unmistakable relation sign. The source comparison from scan017 was supplied by the main reader; Reader C inspected only scan018. The separate final lowercase pi is retained even though the surrounding mathematics may suggest Pi.

Both actual attachment guides were checked. The contr.-to-foncteur guide is already drawn; the pi-prefix guide was inventoried but absent from the accepted TeX and is added. The rising line through the old central parenthesis is a cancellation, not a further guide.

The existing separator was too long relative to the final marginal equivalence. Only its endpoint changes; the double left pointer, functor arrow, raised circle, subscript /F and all marginal wording remain.

The first, diagram and prose Isom forms were compared graphically through the joined serifed I and curled s. The earlier main-reader torsor proof in accepted note N7 is not attributed to this audit and was not repeated. No proof claim arises from this visual confirmation.

The crossed preliminary object formula, tentative older parenthesis, live en fait, two lower cancellations, unexpanded isom and Pi-auto continuation, bare fibre shaft, uncertain point abbreviation and both pencil numerals remain as read. The pencil hand is unnamed; no date is inferred.

Only this page's packet, original, native halves, accepted fragment/report and twelve listed existing crops were visually used, with the authorized contract, reading guidelines and current notation table. No other page image, OCR, external research or TeX compilation was used.
